quick.summary: Why models crash from bad inputs and how to verify data first.
quick.takeaway: Check your data inputs before running the model logic.

beats.line: My model crashed today. A required column was missing. How do I stop this?
Imagine baking a cake. Do you start mixing before checking the eggs?
No, I would check the fridge first.
Right. You verify ingredients early. Code needs the same rule for data.
We set up rules. The model demands a number. The table must provide it.
We call this enforcing a data contract.
Can I just say data checks?
If a check fails, the pipeline halts before the model breaks.
So I write code to inspect the inputs before running my logic.
Exactly. Catch the missing eggs early.

quiz.question: How do you prevent missing inputs from crashing a model?
options: Inspect the data before running logic.
Retrain the model on the errors.
Tell the users to try again.
quiz.explanation: Validating the data first ensures the model only runs when it has everything it needs.

quiz.question: Data checks should happen after the model makes a prediction.
quiz.explanation: Data checks must happen before the model runs to prevent failures.
